_readme: Visual descriptions of PF2e ancestries, for image prompts only.
This lives in the tooling and NOT in lore/ancestries.md on purpose, for two
reasons. The lore file is feeling-first by convention (docs/ancestry-
conventions.md): it says what a people IS, the temperament and disposition,
and carries no appearance at all. And the appearance is not Tyrnarra's to
define anyway; these are Pathfinder 2e ancestries, described by Paizo.
Check anything doubtful against Archives of Nethys.
THREE STATES, and the difference matters:
""         the name alone is enough. An image model already draws this
one correctly, so adding words only spends prompt budget.
This is a FINDING, not a gap: it means somebody checked.
"text..."  the model does not know the ancestry, or knows a different
thing by that name, so the look has to be described.
absent     not catalogued yet. The builder warns rather than guessing.
and see _midjourney_weak: some ancestries Midjourney renders badly no
matter how they are described. The description still stands, because the
other renderers use it; the anchor just has to come from one of them.
`character` text, so they compete with it for the ~150-word Midjourney
budget, and the individual matters more than the species. A spec's own
`character` may contradict the catalog freely: a regional kitsune should not
be forced to look like every other kitsune.
Heritage and cosmology sections of lore/ancestries.md (Layer 1/2/3, mortal
mixes, the old powers' lines) are not ancestries and are not listed here.
LENGTH: as few words as actually work, and that is fewer than it looks.
The first shisk entry ran 31 words and rendered a porcupine; the one that
works is nine: "a humanoid person, with short quills in place of hair".
Two words do the job. PERSON, so the model builds a biped and not an
animal, and the ONE feature that distinguishes the ancestry. Everything
else competes with the individual the spec is actually about.
Lead with the person. An entry that opens on an animal feature renders the
animal, because the ancestry name carries no meaning to anchor it.
A DESCRIPTION REPLACES THE NAME; it is not added to it. An ancestry name
the model cannot read is noise at best, so the prompt carries the
description instead. An entry of "" sends the NAME, because that is what
"the name is enough" means. It does not mean send nothing, which was the
first reading and silently dropped the species out of every kitsune prompt.
A coined compound can beat a sentence: kholo tested best as the single word
"hyenakin", which the model reads compositionally where "kholo" means
nothing to it.
COMPOUNDS BEAT DESCRIPTIONS for animal-derived ancestries. The model reads
<animal>folk and <animal>kin compositionally, which is why ratfolk, catfolk,
lizardfolk and merfolk passed on the name alone: not because Midjourney
knows Pathfinder, but because it can parse rat + folk. kholo tested best as
"hyenakin" for the same reason. Try the compound before writing a sentence.
An ancestry with more than one canon form gets more than one key: anadi is
the true form, a human-sized spider, and anadi-human is the shape they wear
in company. Pick the one the scene actually shows.
FOURTH STATE, null: this ancestry has no generic look at all. A poppet is
whatever it was sewn to be, so there is nothing true to say about poppets
in general; the builder sends nothing and tells the spec to describe this
one in full. Distinct from "", which says the name carries it.
GENRE ANCHOR: an ancestry whose NAME belongs to another genre can be fixed
by naming this one, not by describing features. android drags toward
science fiction, so "a medieval fantasy android" works where every
feature-level attempt failed: plain humans when the tells were subtle, full
machines when they were not. Reach for this when a failure looks like the
wrong SETTING rather than the wrong creature.
The compound suffix is not only -folk and -kin. jotunborn tested best as
"titanborn": -born works too, and the rule is really that a coined compound
beats a sentence whenever the model can read its halves.
_verify: Written from memory of PF2e and not yet checked against Archives of Nethys.
These are the ones worth a look before they reach a render:
_verified: Tested on Midjourney V8.2, 2026-09-14.
CONFIRMED name-is-enough (15): catfolk, dwarf, elf, goblin, halfling,
hobgoblin, human, kitsune, kobold, lizardfolk, minotaur, orc, ratfolk,
skeleton, tengu. Not assumptions any more.
FAILED on the name alone, FIXED by a description (3): gnome rendered a
ceramic garden ornament; merfolk and sprite were wrong. All three verified
correct with the catalog text.
FAILED on the name AND on the description (1): centaur. See
_midjourney_weak.
shisk: CONFIRMED at ten words, person-first. The 31-word version rendered
porcupines. The entry that works is "a humanoid person, with short quills
in place of hair": the person, then the one distinguishing feature.
Still animal-first and likely to fail the same way, untested: tripkee,
tanuki, vanara, nagaji, shoony, anadi. Fix each as it is tested rather
than rewriting them all on one result.
INFERRED from hyenakin, not yet tested: tripkee=frogfolk, vanara=monkeyfolk,
nagaji=snakefolk, shoony=dogfolk, anadi=spiderfolk. anadi is the doubtful
one, being a shapechanger usually seen in humanoid form, so spiderfolk may
render a spider rather than a person. tanuki is left described: it is a real
Japanese word the model may already know, so test the bare name first.
COMPOUNDS TESTED 2026-09-14: hyenafolk, frogfolk (tripkee), monkeyfolk
(vanara), dogfolk (shoony), tanukifolk all correct. hyenakin worked equally
well; -folk kept for consistency.
snakefolk FAILED for nagaji: they are humanoids with serpentine features,
not snake-bodied, and the compound reads toward naga. Person-first instead.
anadi: the spiderfolk render showing humanoids with spider attributes was
most likely CORRECT. Archives of Nethys gives the natural form as humanoid
spiders with distinctive markings, and a separate fully human shape they
assume magically. A spec meeting one in human shape must say so; the
catalog describes the natural form.
nagaji CONFIRMED person-first: "a humanoid person with fine scales and a
snake's head".
anadi: the lore leans SPIDER. PathfinderWiki gives the true form as
human-sized spiders with varied colorations, and Paizo's miniature is titled
Anadi (Spider Form), so spiderfolk was the less accurate render despite
looking more like a character. An anadi NPC met socially is usually in human
shape; use anadi-human for that.
leshy is heritage-varied, so it gets a key per heritage the way anadi gets
one per form: leshy-leaf, -fungus, -fruit, -cactus, -vine, -lotus, -pine,
-root, all confirmed on Archives of Nethys. Plain leshy stays for when the
plant does not matter to the shot. Others may exist in later books; add
them on the same pattern.
leshy CONFIRMED 2026-09-14, base and heritage keys both: the base renders
correctly and swapping the body material (fungus, cactus, lotus) changes
the plant without losing the creature. The heritage-key pattern works.
kashrishi=rhinofolk and ghoran=plantfolk both work: compounds now beat a
description seven times out of seven where one fits.
strix CONFIRMED once trimmed to "a winged person, large feathered wings at
the back". The dark colouring was invented, not canon.
fetchling: dropped "edges that never quite catch the light", a phrase that
reads well and renders as nothing.
goloma FAILED as an abomination: the eyes were put on the head AND
shoulders, which is more than canon and more than an image model can place
tastefully. Retesting with the face only.
poppet leans horror unless handled carefully. "patched where it has worn
through" is a description of decay, so it was doing that on purpose
without meaning to. Retesting plainer.
goloma: first two attempts produced horror because I had the eyes scattered
across a face and then across the head and shoulders. The official art has
a smooth elongated pale head carrying a ROW of round green eyes down each
side, over grey skin and clawed hands. Retesting against that.
poppet is null: there is no default. Every poppet is individually sewn, so
a generic description would be a fiction, and the spec has to do the work.
goloma CONFIRMED from the source text, with two corrections: the eyes are
always EIGHT and are not green. Canon face is an oblong wedge of smooth
chitin resembling a wooden mask, eight gelatinous shining eyes protruding
from it, mouth and jaw beneath the plate, a bony crest on top. Skin ranges
warm brown to ebony, sometimes albino grey-white, so the entry names no
colour and lets the spec choose.
Canon but DELIBERATELY OMITTED: the back of the head and neck carries black
hair filled with thousands of tiny peering eyes that glow and squirm. It is
the most distinctive goloma feature and it is also exactly what produced the
abominations in the first two attempts. Add it in a spec if a scene wants
the horror; keep it out of the default.
awakened animal is null for the poppet reason: an awakened crow and an
awakened badger share nothing a default could describe.
azarketi CONFIRMED. dragonet CONFIRMED as dragonkin: it reads close to a
kobold, and so does the real ancestry, so that is correct rather than a
miss.
automaton: "a humanoid construct" alone is enough; brass, iron, joints and
faceplate over-defined it.
android FAILED as plain humans: "faint circuitry seams" was too faint to
survive. Retesting with glowing circuitry lines and visible joint seams.
fleshwarp is null, joining poppet and awakened animal: each one is warped
differently by whatever made it, so there is no shared look to describe.
wayang was badly wrong. "skin that swallows light" is a rendering
instruction, not an appearance. Source: small and wiry, skin from ivory
white to duskwood black, THICK SHADOWS THAT FLIT AND DANCE ON THE SKIN LIKE
A SECOND LAYER, intricate painted patterns often mistaken for tattoos, long
hair held up in elaborate shell-and-horn headdresses, long scarves or shawls.
The shadow-as-second-skin is the trait that distinguishes them.
vishkanya was NEVER tested from the catalog. Caevan's renders came from his
spec's own character text, not from this entry, so it counted as proven and
was not. The entry also opened on the scaling rather than on a person, the
shape that failed for shisk and kashrishi; rewritten person-first.
automaton CONFIRMED as "a humanoid construct".
vishkanya was wrong: the source has them HUMANLIKE, with ophidian traits
only clear close up. Tall and lithe, small smooth scales in earthy browns
and greens or bright patterns, bright golden eyes with vertical pupils, a
forked tongue, usually dark hair, and they never stop growing so old ones
pass seven feet. "jewel-toned scaling and luminous eyes" oversold all of it.
wayang, second failure: renders came back as tattered scarecrow figures.
"thick shadows moving across the skin like a second layer" is the canon
trait and Midjourney reads it as ragged cloth, and "elaborate shell
headdress" took over the whole silhouette. Both dropped. The shadow may
simply not be renderable; it belongs in a spec if a scene needs it.
android: still wrong, generating plain humans even with glowing circuitry.
Needs its own pass with a reference.
wayang CONFIRMED once the unrenderable parts were dropped: small, dark grey
skin, white painted patterns, long black hair. The canon shadow-as-second-
skin and the shell headdress both had to go.
vishkanya, second failure, overcorrected the other way: small scales plus
vertical pupils plus a forked tongue is three snake traits and renders a
snake person. Canon is humanlike with the traits clear only close up, so
the entry now leads on "human person" and keeps two faint tells.
android CONFIRMED as name-is-enough, after two descriptions failed in
opposite directions. "a synthetic person with glowing circuitry" rendered
plain humans; "a humanoid robot with pale synthetic skin" rendered full
machines; the bare name renders people who happen to be androids, some with
a visible seam or a mechanical limb, which is the register a character
portrait wants.
AND THE PROFILE IS NOT THE PROBLEM. Running the same description with
--profile REMOVED made it worse, not better: glowing neon figures with no
clothing. The profile keeps prompts in character-art register, so do not
reach for dropping it when an entry misbehaves. Hypothesis tested and dead.
android CORRECTION: the bare name is not enough. It gives the right
register, but half the grid came back as plain humans, so it is a coin
flip rather than a pass. Retesting with one quiet tell, "fine synthetic
seams on the skin", avoiding circuitry and glowing, which were the words
that overshot into full machines.
android CONFIRMED as "a medieval fantasy android". Four attempts to
describe its features failed in both directions before the actual problem
turned out to be genre: the word pulls to science fiction, and two words of
setting fix what no amount of seams and circuitry could.
anadi, anadi-human and fetchling all CONFIRMED.
anadi-human renders plain humans, which is the correct answer rather than a
failure: the whole point of the form is that it passes. Its two tells, the
sheen in the eyes and the stiff deliberate movement, do not survive a still
portrait, so the entry effectively reads as "a human person". Kept as
written because it documents what the form is for, but a spec wanting the
wrongness visible has to put it there itself.
athamaru source: fish-like, brightly coloured skin matching their reefs,
frills, barbels and crested fins, flamboyant, and communities share features
so individuals vary a lot. Also a strong pheromone smell, which no portrait
can carry. Trying the compound first on the 7-for-7 record; the fallback
below adds the reef colour and the fins if plain fishfolk comes back drab.
athamaru CONFIRMED as fishfolk. Compounds are 8 for 8.
jotunborn rewritten from source. The old entry had the size and missed the
defining feature entirely: threads of iivlar silk woven along the surface of
the skin, which the source calls their most notable trait and which the art
shows as rows of fine white stitching. Also twice human height, about twelve
feet, thick through the shoulders and neck, skin in pale purples, blues and
light greys. The threads can be made to glow; left out of the default since
that is a thing they do rather than a thing they look like.
jotunborn CONFIRMED as "titanborn", beating the sourced description. Nine
compounds out of nine.
samsaran rewritten from source, and the old entry was substantially
invented. White hair is wrong, the art has dark hair, and "faint markings
across the brow left by lives it does not remember" was fiction on top of
narrative. Canon: blue skin from pale to deepest midnight navy, and
PUPILLESS pallid eyes like the moon. Everything else varies, because a
samsaran carries the features of whatever ancestry it first lived as.
Transparent blood is canon and cannot appear in a portrait.
samsaran CONFIRMED as "a person with blue skin and pale eyes". Pupilless
tips it into horror and pale eyes already carries the moon-like look, so
the word is dropped: another canon trait that reads wrong in a render.
sarangay from source, and the compound beats the description again: a
cowfolk with a gem in the forehead. The head gem is from birth, houses the
soul, and is swapped with a partner for life, so it is the one feature that
must survive. Also canon: 6 to 7 feet, heavily muscled, black eyes with
WHITE CRESCENT pupils, large clawed hands, hooved legs, horns that mark
adulthood at two feet, and gold bangles and nose rings. All left out; the
compound carries the shape and the gem carries the identity.
sarangay CONFIRMED as "a cowfolk with a gem in the forehead".
surki has THREE canon forms, so it takes three keys, the anadi and leshy
pattern again. Larval: a two-foot grub, translucent flesh with luminescent
nodes, round eyeless chitinous head, six legs with heavy front digging
claws. Adult, the form seen on the surface and the default here: roughly
bipedal on two multi-jointed legs, three-fingered claws, two feathery
antennae, two long sensory barbels beside the mandibles, a rounded shape
with rust-brown or orange chitin plates along the back. Evolved, after the
grand metamorphosis: the magical nodes become organs projecting tangible
magic, including glowing wings that defy gravity, which is what the
reference art shows.
gnome: a small fey person about three feet tall, large bright eyes, sharp delicate features, vividly coloured hair, warm living skin
centaur: the upper body of a person rising where a horse's neck would be, joined seamlessly at the waist to a full four-legged horse body
merfolk: a person from the waist up and a long scaled fish tail instead of legs, iridescent, with trailing fins at the hips and forearms
sprite: a tiny fey no taller than a hand, translucent insect wings, sharp delicate features, built to the scale of a flower
anadi: a human-sized spider with bright distinctive colour markings
azarketi: a humanoid person with smooth blue-green skin, webbed hands and gills at the neck
conrasu: a bodiless spirit wearing a carved shell of pale wood and living growth, no face inside the hood, faint light at the seams
fetchling: a person with ash-grey skin, colourless hair, and eyes with no whites
goloma: a humanoid person whose face is a smooth chitin plate like a wooden mask, with eight shining eyes and a bony crest above
leshy: a small plant creature with a body of living plant matter and a simple face
nagaji: a humanoid person with fine scales and a snake's head
samsaran: a person with blue skin and pale eyes
sarangay: a cowfolk with a gem in the forehead
shisk: a humanoid person, with short quills in place of hair
strix: a winged person, large feathered wings at the back
surki: insectfolk with feathery antennae and rust-orange chitin plates on the back
vishkanya: a tall lithe human person with golden eyes with vertical pupils and faint fine scales on the skin
wayang: a small humanoid person with dark grey skin, white painted patterns on the face and arms, and long black hair
yaksha: a nature spirit wearing a person's shape, skin the colour of bark or river stone, small horns or budding growth at the brow
yaoguai: a beast that became a person and kept the evidence: a mostly human shape carrying the ears, eyes or hands of the animal it was

_midjourney_weak.centaur: Midjourney renders centaurs badly with or without the description, and adding one made it worse. Anchor on local FLUX and attach that to the prompt for the rest of the set, the way Harlen Doss and Aldous were done.

anadi-human: a human person, with an odd lovely sheen to the dark eyes and stiff deliberate movements
leshy-leaf: a small plant creature with a body of layered leaves and foliage and a simple face
leshy-fungus: a small plant creature with a body of mushroom caps and pale fungus and a simple face
leshy-fruit: a small plant creature with a body of ripening fruit on the vine and a simple face
leshy-cactus: a small plant creature with a body of spined green cactus and a simple face
leshy-vine: a small plant creature with a body of coiled prehensile vines and a simple face
leshy-lotus: a small plant creature with a body of lotus petals and water lilies and a simple face
leshy-pine: a small plant creature with a body of pine bark and needles and a simple face
leshy-root: a small plant creature with a body of knotted woody roots and a simple face
surki-larva: a two-foot translucent grub with glowing nodes inside it, a round eyeless head, and large digging claws
surki-evolved: insectfolk with large glowing translucent wings and luminous patterns in the chitin
